metadata.title: What It Sees, And What It Misses
metadata.greeting_note: ATTRIBUTION OVERRIDE (established 2026-07-31, carried forward from 09-04-01 and 09-04-02): hosted by Sai in his own name, not by Liam-in-for-Bear. Voice stays Kokoro am_onyx. B00 says 'This is Sai'; B09 signs off 'Sai.' The IN-FOR-BEAR LAW of WEEKLY-VIDEO-GUIDE.md is deliberately suspended for this series.
metadata.note: WEEKLY PROGRESS REEL for the loon-detector project, week of 2026-09-11. NO TEAMMATE IS NAMED ANYWHERE, by the author's explicit instruction: collaborators appear as 'we' and 'the team', never by name, in narration, on-screen text, SOURCES.md and PEDAGOGY.md alike. THE WEEK, as reported by the author: the first iteration of LoonNet is trained on 106 images and validated against ~26 held out from the same repository; he supplied two YOLO prediction mosaics, val_batch0_pred.jpg and val_batch1_pred.jpg; he flagged three weaknesses (duplicate detections, one section of land read as a loon, and a training set that is too small); a dedicated false-positive evaluation has NOT been run; precision/recall/accuracy from the model are NOT yet available and are promised before the team meeting. He also proposed an order for seven application features and recommended keeping CVAT rather than building an annotation tool. THROUGH-LINE: the seven failures are not one failure. Four distinct causes sit behind them, and only some are fixed by more data — which is why the reel refuses to average them into a single score. FIGURES — READ THIS BEFORE CHANGING ANY NUMBER ON SCREEN. Author-supplied: 106 training images, ~26 held out. Printed by the YOLO plotter in the supplied mosaics and therefore quotable verbatim: every per-frame confidence (0.3 ... 0.9) and the two class names, 'common loon' and 'non loon'. EVERYTHING ELSE IS A HAND AUDIT performed by reading the two sheets cell by cell: 26 populated frames (16 + 10), 28 loons visible, 19 frames clean, 7 frames with a defect, ~26 of 28 loons found. These are NOT model metrics. No precision, recall, mAP, F1, IoU, epoch count, image size, batch size or confidence threshold appears anywhere in the reel, because none were supplied. B07's fourth artifact line states the hand-audit caveat in full and must not be cut. A FOURTH WEAKNESS IS ON SCREEN THAT THE AUTHOR DID NOT LIST: in val_batch1_pred.jpg, web_20260818_0076.jpg shows two loons in fog and the model returned no detection at all. The author reviewed this and approved including it. TWO CLASSES, NOT ONE: 'non loon0.8' is visible in val_batch0_pred.jpg r4c4, so this model was trained to reject as well as accept. That is why B01 carries two class chips and why B05's ghostText says the false-positive test comes first. ONE CLAIM DELIBERATELY NOT MADE: val_batch1_pred.jpg r4c2 (web_20260818_0107.jpg) appears to show a Black Guillemot on a rock, detected as a common loon at 0.7. It is NOT counted as a false positive anywhere and is not on any plate — the identification is not certain enough to put on screen. It is logged in SOURCES.md as a data-quality item for the author to verify. ILLUSTRATE LAW: Claude UI at B00, B08 and the verdict/outro only. Body beats run ChipGrid -> STILL -> DivergentFates -> STILL -> BinaryBranch -> ChipGrid; no two consecutive beats share a pattern. SHORTS / 9:16: ClaudeScienceLayerStack and ClaudeScienceSourceFlow — the guide's default B01/B02 patterns — have NO registered 916 sibling and are avoided for that reason alone. Every Remotion pattern used here does have one (ClaudeComposerAsk916, ClaudeScienceChipGrid916, DivergentFates916, BinaryBranch916, ClaudeVerdictArtifact916, LogoOutro916), so shorts.py rewires with no new TSX. B02 and B04 are user media and would otherwise be centre-cut; both carry hand-composed pantry/<beat>-916.png plates from make_plates.py and both hold rather than pan. B06 is dropped from the short (--drop B06): the 9:16 cut is model results only. NARRATION CARRIES NO POSITIONAL REFERENCE ('top left', 'the third one') because the same mp3 plays over both the landscape and portrait plates and the cell order differs. B04's narration says 'the first' rather than 'top left' for exactly this reason. typeScale 1.4 on the two deck patterns, which were authored against a 1280x720 stage; the 916 siblings take {data} only and ignore it harmlessly. Deck-pattern label and detail strings are kept under ~42 characters — fixed-x SVG text does not reflow, so a long string overprints silently and Remotion still exits 0. OUTRO: LogoOutro, not ClaudeTitleOutro, whose handle is hardcoded to @NikBearBrown. B09 narration is 8 words so it finishes inside the 4.0s card before its fade — see the _contract_note on that beat. `./art run` will print a SKIN LINT line asking for ClaudeTitleOutro; it is wrong for this channel and is expected.
metadata.voice_note: metadata.voice (legacy) is deliberately ABSENT. build_safety.default_voice treats it as an alias for the Kokoro voice id and refuses the build when it disagrees with voice_kokoro — and this series used to set voice='NikBearBrown', a persona name, not a voice id. The persona is carried by channel, folder_chip and greeting_note instead. 09-04-01 and 09-04-02 still carry the old pair and will hit the same refusal if their audio is ever regenerated.

beats.narration_text: This is the first LoonNet. A hundred and six images to train on, twenty-six held back to test it. This is Sai. Before I tell you it works, I want to do what a results page never does on its own — go frame by frame, count what it got wrong, and say that number out loud.

show.event: the ask types in — the week's question, not the week's summary
the three result lines land under it, headline first
the last line is the one the rest of the reel has to earn

props.segment: What It Sees, And What It Misses
props.command: LoonNet, first iteration. 106 images trained, 26 held back and never seen. Here are its predictions. Don't tell me it looks promising — go frame by frame, tell me what it gets wrong, how often, and which of those are the same mistake wearing two names.
output: two classes — common loon, non loon

beats.narration_text: The training set is a hundred and six images, pooled from the web and from our own cameras. Twenty-six more were held back, and the model never saw them. Four capture paths are in there — web stills, a Nikon from shore, a drone over open water, and a phone. And two classes, not one: common loon, and non loon.

show.event: the two set sizes land first — what it learned from, what it was tested on
four capture paths fill in, each a different distance to the bird
two class labels close the grid — this model was taught what is NOT a loon

props.sparkLine: THE FIRST LOONNET · WHAT WENT IN
props.caption: Capture paths read off the filename prefixes — web_, nikon_, dji_, iphone_

beats.narration_text: This is what came back. Every blue box is a detection on a picture the model had never seen, and the number beside it is its confidence — nought point three at the low end, nought point nine at the high. Now look at the range. In one frame the bird fills half the picture. In another, four dark pixels on open water.

show.event: the full sheet holds — sixteen frames at once, boxes already drawn
the eye takes the easy cells first, where the bird fills its frame
then the hard ones, where the box is smaller than its own caption
the caption states what the plate is and how many frames it shows

still.composed_from: author's own YOLO prediction mosaic (data/val_batch0_pred.jpg, staged to images/B02-source.jpg at 1920x1280, a 4x4 sheet of 480x320 cells), composed to 3840x2160 by make_plates.py
still.note: HOLD, not kenburns: the range across all sixteen cells IS the beat, and compile.py's zoompan pushes ~8% outward, which clips the outer cells. Portrait override at pantry/B02-916.png — eight of the sixteen cells re-tiled 2x4, NOT shorts.py's centre cut, which keeps the middle 37.5% of the width and would halve two columns. Cells are screened by make_plates.py --audit in BOTH directions: a cell must neither inherit a label fragment from its left neighbour nor have its own caption sliced at its right edge. That excludes all six column-3 and column-4 shore frames, which are the most distant subjects in the batch — spent deliberately rather than shown truncated.

beats.narration_text: And mostly, it works. Of the twenty-six frames I went through by hand, nineteen came back clean — the bird found once, boxed, nothing invented. For a first iteration on a hundred and six images, that is a real result. But the seven that failed are not seven copies of one problem. They are four different ones.

show.event: one model at the start of the track — the same weights for every frame
the split opens on the only question that matters: what came back
the upper track climbs — nineteen frames clean, which is most of them
the lower track falls, and it does not fall for one reason

tracks.label: 7 frames
notes: a reed bed called a loon

beats.narration_text: Here they are. The first should reassure you — a drone frame, two birds a few pixels across, both found. Then the failures. One bird, three overlapping boxes, counted three times. A reed bed boxed as a loon, and a duck beside it called one at nought point three. And two loons in fog, where it returned nothing.

show.event: four panels hold at once — one success, three failures
the drone frame reads first: two birds of a few pixels, both boxed
then the duplicate, then the reed bed, in terracotta
the fog frame closes it — two loons, and no box anywhere

still.composed_from: four cells lifted from data/val_batch0_pred.jpg and data/val_batch1_pred.jpg by make_plates.py, composed to 3840x2160
still.note: HOLD, not kenburns — four panels, no single subject to push toward. One of the four is a SUCCESS on purpose: a failure plate showing only failures is an argument, not evidence. Portrait override at pantry/B04-916.png stacks the same four panels 1x4, left-aligned so each image shares an edge with the caption naming it. Every panel names its source file so any claim in the narration walks back to a frame.

beats.narration_text: Those are worth separating. Double-counting is not a data problem — it is a threshold, one setting governing how hard overlapping boxes get merged, and more images will not touch it. The fog frame and the reed bed are data problems. So: which lever first? Pull both at once and we learn nothing about either.

show.event: the seven failed frames pose the question as one fork
the data branch: slower, and it does not touch double-counting
the threshold branch: one setting, and it lands today
the resolver refuses the merge — change both and neither reads

data.question: Grow the dataset, or tune the detector?

branches.label: More images first
branches.detail: widen the set until hard frames are covered

branches.label: Tune overlap first
branches.detail: merge overlapping boxes before adding data

resolver.label: They do not fix the same frames
resolver.detail: double-counting is a setting; the fog frame is missing data — change both in one pass and neither result is readable

data.ghostText: and the false-positive test comes before either

beats.narration_text: Separately — the feature list. Seven capabilities are on the table, and I would order them by effort against impact rather than by appetite. Detection first, because it exists. Then counting, which is this same model with a rule on top. Then blurring, then the acoustic classifier, then the three habitat models, which need data we have not collected. And one thing to take off the list: we already annotate in CVAT, so we should not be building an annotation tool of our own.

show.event: detection lands first because it already exists
counting and blurring follow — near-term, and cheap on top of detection
the four habitat and acoustic models sit below, waiting on data
the two annotation chips close it — one tool we keep, one we do not build

props.caption: A proposal to open the meeting with, not a decision already taken

cut_policy.why: The 9:16 cut is model results only. Seven ordered items plus two annotation chips cannot be read on a phone, and this is meeting material rather than a result. shorts.py is run with --drop B06.

beats.narration_text: So: one page. The first LoonNet works on most of what it sees. Nineteen frames of twenty-six clean, counted by hand. Four frames double-counted, one boxed a reed bed, one missed two birds in fog. And these are my counts off the sheets, not a validation run. The real precision and recall come from the model, before the meeting.

show.event: the page opens on what was trained and what was held back
the hand-audit line lands — nineteen of twenty-six
the four failure modes, named separately
the caveat closes the page and is not a footnote

props.artifactTitle: What It Sees, And What It Misses
artifactLines: The first LoonNet is trained: 106 images in, 26 held back and never seen. It returned predictions on all 26, at confidences between 0.3 and 0.9.
Hand audit of those 26 frames: 19 came back clean — the bird found once, boxed, nothing invented. Around 26 of the 28 loons visible were found.
Seven frames failed, in four distinct ways: four counted one bird more than once, one boxed a reed bed as a loon, one called a duck a loon at 0.3, and one returned nothing on two loons in fog.

These are hand counts read off the two batch sheets — NOT a validation run. Precision, recall and mAP come from the model itself before the team meeting, and the dedicated false-positive test has not been run yet.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. If you have a first detector of your own, try this. Don't open the metrics. Open the prediction sheet and sort every mistake into piles by cause — not by how bad it looked. Then count the piles. That number is how many problems you actually have, and it is almost never one.

show.event: the handoff prompt types in, ready to paste
the emphasis lands on CAUSE, not on severity
the ask ends on the part a metric cannot answer

props.command: Take a detection model I just trained and its validation prediction sheet. Ignore the metrics. Go frame by frame, list every wrong box, and group them by CAUSE — duplicate, false positive, miss. Then tell me how many distinct problems I have, and which of them more training data will not fix.

beats.narration_text: What it sees, and what it misses. Sai.

show.event: the humanitarians mark springs in on the cream ground
the handle settles beneath it
the mark holds, then the card closes
